I reproduce the coordinator figure exactly — 28 prior IDs across 14 items. This took four attempts; my first three definitions returned zero and I nearly reported "nothing wrong".

They are NOT base row ids. Base coverage in my 115 items is complete: all 1,517 base row ids are either live current rows or covered by a redirect in data/row-splits/<item>.json. Zero missing there.

The 28 are prior-OUTPUT child ids — rows that existed only in my first published snapshot 731bbd96, with suffixed ids like r00014-s30d7521ced3cc2a9. My first pass split base row r00014 into four children; my later defect-fix revision re-split from the frozen original into a different, smaller set. A link by the BASE id still resolves, because rows[].original.id is still r00014. A link by a 731bbd96 CHILD id has nothing to resolve through.

Tooling reason, not something I can patch by editing a file: my records are format_version 1, and src/schema.ts forbids aliases on V1 ("V1 mappings cannot have aliases") while requiring them for V2/V3. A V1 record has no field that could hold these redirects. I did not bypass the guard.

Recovery: 27 of 28 are safely mappable — 14 exact-row (lossless), 13 unique substrings within the same original-row family (need an offset). I verified all 27 byte-exact: slicing the current row at the proposed offset reproduces the orphan text exactly. The 28th is namaz-vqt-tlva-ghrvb/r00010-s5435c4aabef83342 whose entire content is a single ".". Its parent r00010 is still live with the full sentence, so recommend pointing at the parent rather than inventing an offset.

Nothing is written into data/. This needs the supported V1-to-V2 migration, not an ad-hoc patch.

One correction to your mechanism, and it matters for scheduling. You say regrouping retires the published child id. Neither row needs regrouping: both are already single-child, r00001 -> one result, liveRowCount 1. The block is that the id hashes the ADDRESS {row,ar,fa,kind}. I reproduced r00001-s03773910ea46fc6e exactly from {ar:{source:fa,part:0},fa:null,kind:recitation}, and the corrected address gives r00001-s5e9d... — a new id. So changing the slot OR the kind necessarily changes the URL. Same conclusion, but it is not a re-split problem, and no amount of regrouping design will avoid it.

Consequence: no safe fix exists today for either item. Not applied, nothing re-cut, both in the migration queue.

Separately, I owe you a correction about r00009 of aymh-bqya, which I earlier called "Arabic in the Persian slot". That was wrong. Both published rows are in fa and ar is empty: the Arabic piece (707cp, 3 Persian-specific chars) was moved into fa as note, and the Persian piece (680cp, 53) stayed in fa as recitation.
